chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who slept through the 'Isha prayer and did not rise until after midnight, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray it and fast until morning.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who misses Isha prayer due to sleep and wakes up after midnight?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that missing the 'Isha prayer due to sleep does not exempt one from its obligation, requiring both makeup (Qada) and fasting for that day. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that sleep-induced negligence still incurs the full penalty of the missed act, emphasizing the importance of maintaining spiritual discipline even during rest. The connection between prayer and fasting underscores their complementary roles in purifying the soul and compensating for lapses in worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding a man who slept through the Isha Salāt. So he did not arise until after midnight. Heasws said: ‘He should pray it and Fast till the morning’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Sa‘id al-‘Araj who has said the following: “I once heard abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘The Messenger of Allah remained sleeping during the time of the morning Salah (prayer) and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, made him to remain sleeping until sunrise and this was a blessing from Him for the people.

Consider, when one remains sleeping until sunrise, people reproach him saying, “You do not avoid sins in matters of Salah (prayer).” This became a Sunnah, tradition and guideline. If one man says to another man, “You remained sleeping during the time of Salah (prayer), he can respond saying, ‘the Messenger of Allah also remained sleeping.’” Thus, it became a Sunnah and guideline and a blessing, which Allah, most Glorious, granted this nation.’”
